item.title: After Abbas: Who Gets Power First—and Who Gets to Keep It?
item.description: Palestinian rules point to Hussein al-Sheikh as temporary president if the office becomes vacant today. But permanent power is supposed to come from voters—and three promised ballots collide with competing laws, new appointments, occupation, fragmentation and deep public distrust.

item.title: When the Internet Goes Dark: Why Bitchat Matters for Palestinians
item.description: Palestinians know better than almost anyone on earth what it means for the internet to disappear. item.title: The Forty Percent Toll: In Gaza, Accessing Your Own Money Can Cost Nearly Half of It
item.description: In Gaza, the price of your own money can run to forty percent. That is the fee human rights monitors report Palestinians are paying to informal cash brokers simply to convert the balance in their bank account — money they already own — into the physical banknotes needed to buy food, water, or medicine.

item.title: Locked Out of Their Own Money: The West Bank's Cash Crisis and the Case for Financial Freedom
item.description: In the occupied West Bank, money itself has become a front line. Gas stations have refused customers' banknotes because their banks will no longer accept deposits. Businesses pay to guard cash they cannot bank. And the institution responsible for Palestinian monetary stability says openly that the system has been turned into a weapon. item.title: In Gaza, Twenty Young Volunteers Train to Preserve Palestinian Memory
item.description: Twenty young volunteers in Gaza completed the first training workshop held by Mena'a Ltd on Sunday, a session devoted to field documentation, occupational safety and digital security — skills the organization says are the foundation of responsible documentation work.
